# Northstar rollout status

Reporting window: 3-7 February
Owner: Platform Enablement
Overall state: amber, trending green

## Executive summary

The new workspace provisioning path is active for internal teams in two regions. Median setup time fell from eleven minutes to three minutes after the image cache was moved closer to the runners. The remaining risk is not capacity; it is the uneven age of customer-managed DNS records. Eight accounts still point at the retired validation hostname.

| Workstream | Lead | State | Evidence | Next checkpoint |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| account import | Mina | done | 1,842 records reconciled | archive old export |
| runner pools | Theo | healthy | p95 queue 18 seconds | add weekend alarm |
| DNS cutover | Inez | at risk | 8 stale CNAME records | contact account owners |
| support training | Ravi | in review | handbook draft approved | record walkthrough |

Completed this week:

- Added an idempotency key to workspace creation so a browser retry cannot produce a duplicate tenant.
- Backfilled ownership labels for accounts created before the billing system supplied a team identifier.
- Published a dry-run command that lists planned mutations without applying them.
- Split the availability graph by region and machine class.

Open decisions:

1. Keep the compatibility redirect until all eight DNS records move, even though it complicates certificate renewal.
2. Decide whether suspended trials belong in the nightly reconciliation job.
3. Choose a single source for customer display names; the sales export and billing ledger disagree on punctuation.

## Risk register

| Risk | Likelihood | Impact | Mitigation |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| stale DNS prevents callback validation | medium | high | preserve redirect and alert per account |
| large imports exceed job lease | low | medium | checkpoint every 250 rows |
| retry storm saturates audit writes | low | high | bounded exponential delay and circuit break |

No data loss was observed. Every imported row can be traced to an immutable batch identifier, and the rollback tool has been exercised against a synthetic tenant.

# Harbor 2.8.0 release notes

This release focuses on predictable exports, clearer operator feedback, and smaller cold-start costs.

## Added

- A preview subcommand that prints the destination, selected filters, and estimated row count.
- Support for newline-delimited JSON alongside the existing CSV exporter.
- Human-readable explanations for policy denials, including the rule name and remediation link.
- A health endpoint that distinguishes startup, ready, draining, and failed states.

## Changed

- Configuration files are now merged in this order: system defaults, repository settings, user settings, then command-line flags.
- Empty date ranges return an empty collection instead of a validation error.
- Temporary files use the same filesystem as the destination so the final rename remains atomic.
- Progress output moves to stderr, leaving stdout safe for pipes.

## Fixed

- Quoted CSV fields containing carriage returns no longer create phantom records on Windows.
- A cancelled upload releases its concurrency permit before retry scheduling.
- The terminal renderer measures visible width after removing color escape sequences.
- Cache entries now include the normalized locale in their key.

## Upgrade guidance

Operators using a custom wrapper should check whether it assumes progress messages arrive on stdout. The deprecated HARBOR_LEGACY_DATES switch remains accepted for one release but prints a warning. Existing export manifests require no migration.

Before deployment:

- run a preview against one representative project;
- compare row counts with the previous stable binary;
- verify that the service account can create and rename files in the destination;
- capture a rollback manifest.

## Compatibility

The command-line interface supports Linux and macOS on current x64 and arm64 machines. The library build targets maintained JavaScript runtimes. Network storage is supported when it provides atomic rename semantics.

# Ledger inventory API

The inventory service reports stock positions, reservations, and inbound shipments for a warehouse. Quantities are integers in the smallest sellable unit.

Base URL: https://inventory.example.test/v2

## Authentication

Send a short-lived bearer token in the Authorization header. Tokens are scoped to an organization and one or more facilities. Requests without a facility claim receive 403 even when the organization matches.

## List positions

GET /facilities/{facilityId}/positions

Query parameters:

| Name | Type | Required | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| cursor | string | no | opaque continuation cursor |
| limit | integer | no | page size from 1 through 250 |
| sku | string | no | exact normalized SKU |
| changed_after | timestamp | no | lower bound, exclusive |

Example response:

```json
{
  "items": [
    {
      "sku": "TEA-ASSAM-250",
      "on_hand": 86,
      "reserved": 12,
      "available": 74,
      "location": "A-03-17",
      "revision": 42
    }
  ],
  "next_cursor": "cD00MiZzPV..."
}
```

## Reserve stock

POST /facilities/{facilityId}/reservations

The Idempotency-Key header is required. Repeating an identical request returns the original reservation. Reusing the key with different fields returns 409.

Possible errors:

- 400 malformed JSON or an invalid quantity;
- 404 unknown facility or SKU;
- 409 insufficient unreserved stock, stale revision, or conflicting idempotency key;
- 429 facility write budget exhausted.

Clients should treat the error code as stable and the prose message as diagnostic. A retry-after value, when present, is measured in whole seconds.

## Consistency

Position reads are monotonic within a cursor walk. A reservation becomes visible to subsequent reads after its transaction commits. Webhook delivery is at least once, so consumers must deduplicate by event_id.

# Fieldnote command-line guide

Fieldnote turns a directory of interview notes into a searchable local catalog. It does not upload recordings or transcripts.

## Install

```sh
npm install --global fieldnote-cli
fieldnote --version
```

## Create a catalog

```sh
fieldnote init ./research
fieldnote add ./research/notes --author "Product Research"
fieldnote build ./research --format sqlite
```

The add command accepts Markdown and plain text. Front matter is optional. When a document has no explicit title, the first non-empty heading is used, followed by the filename.

## Search

```sh
fieldnote search ./research "renewal reminder" --since 2025-01-01
fieldnote search ./research "mobile checkout" --tag usability --json
```

Search terms are case-insensitive. Quoted phrases must occur in order. Multiple tag flags are combined with AND semantics.

## Configuration

Fieldnote reads fieldnote.toml from the catalog root:

```toml
[catalog]
language = "en"
follow_symlinks = false
ignore = ["archive/**", "**/*.draft.md"]

[index]
stemming = true
max_file_bytes = 2000000
```

## Backup and repair

The source notes remain authoritative. The generated index may be deleted and rebuilt at any time. Use fieldnote doctor to check for unreadable files, duplicate document keys, and index schema drift.

Exit codes:

| Code | Meaning |
| ---: | --- |
| 0 | command completed |
| 2 | invalid arguments |
| 3 | source file could not be read |
| 4 | catalog needs a rebuild |
| 8 | unexpected internal failure |

For automation, prefer --json and inspect the top-level status field instead of parsing terminal prose.

# Launch readiness meeting

Date: 12 March, 14:00 UTC
Facilitator: Lena
Attendees: application, infrastructure, support, security, analytics

## Goal

Confirm whether the recurring invoice reminder can move from staff-only traffic to ten percent of eligible accounts.

## Evidence reviewed

- Delivery success was 99.72% across 184,000 test messages.
- The unsubscribe path completed in under 400 ms at p95.
- Support reviewed all new message templates in English, French, and German.
- The analytics event matches the production naming registry.
- A restored database snapshot reproduced the same eligibility count as the live read replica.

## Discussion

Infrastructure noted that the scheduled burst begins four minutes after the hourly warehouse compaction. Moving the reminder job by ten minutes avoids overlapping CPU peaks. Product accepted the delay because messages are grouped by the recipient's local morning, not by an exact minute.

Security asked whether an account administrator can preview the final recipient list. The current preview shows counts by locale but not addresses. The group agreed that exporting addresses would create unnecessary handling risk; support can investigate an individual message by delivery identifier.

## Decisions

1. Proceed with ten percent traffic on Tuesday.
2. Hold at ten percent for twenty-four hours before considering fifty percent.
3. Stop automatically if hard bounces exceed 1.5% over any rolling thirty-minute window.
4. Keep the former reminder workflow disabled but deployable until the experiment ends.

## Actions

| Owner | Action | Due |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Omar | shift scheduler window | Monday |
| Priya | add bounce-rate stop rule | Monday |
| Jules | publish support lookup steps | Tuesday |
| Lena | record go or no-go outcome | Tuesday |

Parking lot: consolidate template preview tools after launch; it is not required for this rollout.

# Raster pipeline benchmark

## Objective

Measure the effect of chunk size and worker count on a batch that reads source photographs, applies orientation, produces two thumbnails, and writes checksums.

Host: 8 performance cores, 32 GiB memory, local NVMe
Dataset: 6,400 JPEG files, 18.7 GiB total
Runs: five measured repetitions after one warm-up

| Workers | Chunk | Median wall time | p95 item time | Peak RSS | Errors |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 2 | 8 | 311.4 s | 182 ms | 1.2 GiB | 0 |
| 4 | 8 | 174.8 s | 201 ms | 2.1 GiB | 0 |
| 6 | 16 | 132.6 s | 226 ms | 3.5 GiB | 0 |
| 8 | 16 | 129.9 s | 308 ms | 4.9 GiB | 0 |
| 8 | 32 | 128.7 s | 421 ms | 7.8 GiB | 0 |

Six workers with sixteen-item chunks is the recommended default. The two faster configurations save less than four seconds while increasing tail latency and memory pressure substantially.

## Notes

The checksum stage was deliberately included because production verifies every derived file before publishing its manifest. Disabling checksums improves the headline by about seven percent but measures a different workflow.

The first run after reboot was excluded. Filesystem cache state was then held constant by rotating input order without evicting data. CPU frequency remained within three percent across measured runs.

## Follow-up

- Repeat on network-attached storage with the same manifest.
- Record energy use on the small office server.
- Separate decode time from resize time using trace spans.
- Add one corpus containing unusually tall images.

Raw samples:

```csv
workers,chunk,run,seconds,peak_rss_mb
4,8,1,176.2,2104
4,8,2,174.8,2121
6,16,1,132.6,3548
6,16,2,133.1,3562
8,32,1,128.7,7974
```

# Queue delay incident review

Incident window: 09:18-10:07 UTC
Severity: SEV-2
Affected system: outbound document conversion

## Impact

Jobs continued to be accepted, but the oldest waiting job reached twenty-six minutes. Approximately 7,300 conversions completed late. No input documents or generated files were lost.

## Timeline

- 09:18: deploy introduced a new metadata lookup before job admission.
- 09:23: cache miss rate rose from 4% to 61%.
- 09:29: queue-age warning fired; on-call compared worker saturation and database load.
- 09:36: feature flag disabled the lookup for newly admitted jobs.
- 09:44: backlog began shrinking.
- 10:07: oldest-job age returned below the five-minute objective.

## Root cause

The lookup cache used the caller's mixed-case organization key, while the database returned a lowercase canonical key. Successful lookups were stored under a value that subsequent requests did not use. The database handled the extra reads, but admission workers spent most of their leases waiting for connections.

## Contributing factors

- The load test reused one lowercase organization key and never exercised case variation.
- The queue alarm measured depth but not age until a recent dashboard update.
- The feature was enabled globally instead of by a small account cohort.

## Corrective actions

| Priority | Work | Verification |
| --- | --- | --- |
| P0 | normalize keys at the cache boundary | mixed-case unit table |
| P0 | cap lookup concurrency per worker | saturation test |
| P1 | canary metadata changes by account | rollout checklist |
| P1 | alert on connection wait time | forced pool exhaustion |
| P2 | expose cache-key cardinality | dashboard review |

The response was effective once the lookup flag was identified. Future drills should practice detecting a latency regression when throughput remains nonzero.

# Archive migration handbook

## Purpose

This runbook moves completed case files from the primary document store to the lower-cost archive tier while retaining searchable metadata. It is written for the quarterly migration window and assumes the operator has read-only access to production until the approval step.

## Preconditions

- The candidate query has been reviewed by the records owner.
- Legal holds have been synchronized within the last hour.
- The archive bucket reports healthy replication in both target regions.
- A restore drill using the current tool version completed during the last thirty days.
- The change ticket names an operator and a separate approver.

Never infer eligibility from a folder name. A case is eligible only when its state is closed, its retention start is older than the policy threshold, and no active hold references the case identifier.

## Phase 1: inventory

Run the planner without write credentials:

```sh
archive-plan --policy policies/quarterly.yaml   --as-of 2026-03-31   --output work/candidates.ndjson   --summary work/candidates-summary.json
```
